RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-F65CAC945B-43805
Member: Skyler Grant, Member ID W988301014
Date of Notice: 2026-08-03
Service Denied: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Stated Reason for Denial: "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity"

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-03. I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in that notice (by 2027-01-30), and I am requesting reversal of the denial and approval of the requested surgery.

1. The denial notice does not identify the specific medical policy applied to my case.

The notice states only that the procedure "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity," without naming or attaching the specific medical policy, clinical guideline, or criteria set the reviewer used. I have not been able to locate a MassHealth fee-for-service "Guidelines for Medical Necessity Determination" document specific to hip arthroscopy; MassHealth's published guideline list includes documents for other orthopedic procedures (e.g., knee arthroscopy, knee arthroplasty) but does not include one for hip arthroscopy. Separately, MassHealth's own published guidance states that "[p]roviders serving members enrolled in a MassHealth-contracted accountable care partnership plan (ACPP), managed care organization (MCO), integrated care organization (ICO), senior care organization (SCO), or program of all-inclusive care for the elderly (PACE) should refer to the ACPP's, MCO's, ICO's, SCO's or PACE's medical policies for covered services." If my coverage is administered through such a plan, I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, a copy of the exact policy, criteria set (including any InterQual or MCG criteria and the specific version/date used), and the reviewer's individualized rationale that were applied to deny this request, so that I and my surgeon can respond point-by-point. I am not able to quote that specific criteria language here because it has not yet been provided to me.

2. To the extent the plan is applying clinical coverage criteria similar to those published for hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) by at least one MassHealth-contracted plan, my clinical record satisfies those criteria.

One MassHealth-contracted plan's publicly available "Hip Arthroscopy for Femoroacetabular Impingement" Clinical Coverage Criteria document states that the plan's criteria are used because "MassHealth does not have Medical Necessity Guidelines for hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement," and that under that policy, hip arthroscopy for FAI is excluded from coverage only in limited circumstances, including: "Treatment of asymptomatic patients with incidental findings of FAI," and "in the presence of advanced osteoarthritis defined as Tönnis grade 2 or 3, or joint space of < 2 mm." My case falls into neither excluded category, and if this or a substantially similar criteria set was applied to my request, the following facts from my prior authorization packet directly rebut the denial:

- I am not asymptomatic. I have had 14 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest, with sharp anterosuperior groin pain on sitting and pivoting, and I am unable to run or squat.
- Physical examination on file documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- MRI arthrogram of the hip dated 2026-06-23 documents an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees — objective, non-incidental radiographic and clinical correlation of symptomatic FAI, not an "incidental finding."
- The same 2026-06-23 MRI arthrogram documents joint space preserved and Tönnis grade 0 — the opposite of the "advanced osteoarthritis" (Tönnis grade 2 or 3, or joint space < 2 mm) that the above-quoted exclusion describes. My imaging affirmatively places me outside that exclusion.
- I have completed and failed a substantial trial of conservative management prior to requesting surgery: 16 weeks (2026-03-02 to 2026-06-22) of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, totaling 18 completed visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note; 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-04 that provided only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker — none of which are described anywhere in the material I have reviewed as a barrier to surgery.
- My treating orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Duval, has evaluated me, correlated my symptoms and exam findings with the MRI arthrogram results, and determined that arthroscopic treatment (CPT 29914) is indicated after this conservative course has failed.

3. Requested action.

Because (a) I have not been shown the specific criteria the plan used to deny this request, and (b) my documented clinical course does not fall within the only exclusions I have been able to identify in a comparable, publicly available MassHealth-contracted plan's hip arthroscopy criteria, I ask that the plan:

1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29914 as requested by Dr. Duval; or, in the alternative,
2. Provide the specific medical policy, criteria set, and individualized clinical rationale used to deny this request, so that I may supplement this appeal within any remaining appeal window.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of: the physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-02 to 2026-06-22, 18 visits); medication and injection records (NSAID trial and 2026-05-04 corticosteroid injection); the 2026-06-23 MRI arthrogram report; and Dr. Duval's clinical notes and letter of medical necessity.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me and Dr. Duval's office of the outcome in writing. If you have any questions or need additional records, please contact me at [phone number] or [email address], or my surgeon's office at [provider office phone/fax].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Skyler Grant
Member ID: W988301014

cc: Dr. Duval, Orthopedic Surgery, [Practice Name/Address/Fax]

Enclosures: Physical therapy discharge note; medication/injection records; MRI arthrogram report (2026-06-23); surgeon's letter of medical necessity

[Note: This letter does not attribute any policy language to the plan named in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination other than what is expressly quoted above from a publicly available MassHealth-contracted plan's Hip Arthroscopy for Femoroacetabular Impingement Clinical Coverage Criteria document; if that document is not, in fact, the criteria applied to this member, the quoted passages should be understood as illustrative of comparable published criteria, not as an admission of the plan's own policy language, and the plan should still be asked to provide its own applicable criteria as requested in Section 1 above.]
